questionText:
Match the analytical components of L.P. Vidyarthi's 'Sacred Complex' in List-I with their ethnographic examples from Hindu Gaya in List-II:

List I:
(A) Sacred Geography
(B) Sacred Performances
(C) Sacred Specialists
(D) Sacred Patrons / Pilgrims

List II:
(I) Gayawal Pandas (hereditary pilgrim guides, priests, barbers, shrine attendants)
(II) Devout Hindus from all linguistic regions of India performing ancestral rites
(III) Falgu River, Pretshila Hill, Akshayavat tree, and Vishnupad Temple complex
(IV) Pinda-dana (offering rice/barley balls to ancestors), shraddha ceremonies, and holy river ablutions

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.

options.text: A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Sacred Geography is physical shrines (III); Sacred Performances are pinda-dana rites (IV); Sacred Specialists are Gayawal priests (I); Patrons are pilgrims (II).
Hence, Option D is correct.
Hence, option (B) is the correct match.

questionText: What technological innovation in hunting weaponry appeared during the Middle Paleolithic / Middle Stone Age?

options.text: Hafting stone points onto wooden spear shafts using cordage and mastic resin, creating lethal composite thrusting spears

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Composite Tools in Middle Paleolithic (Archaeological Anthropology):
Neanderthals and MSA humans invented composite weapons: hafting triangular Levallois/Mousterian points onto wooden spears for close-quarters big game hunting.
Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.

topic: Engraved Ostrich Eggshell Beads at Patne
questionText: At the Upper Paleolithic site of Patne in the Jalgaon district of Maharashtra, archaeologist S.A. Sali discovered:

options.text: A live ostrich living in a domestic poultry farm
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: A complete Roman temple built of marble
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: A steel railway track from ancient India
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

options.text: Engraved ostrich eggshells and disc beads radiocarbon-dated to approximately 25,000 BP, proving symbolic body ornamentation
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT principle for Engraved Ostrich Eggshell Beads at Patne.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Archaeological Anthropology (Engraved Ostrich Eggshell Beads at Patne):
Engraved ostrich eggshells and disc beads radiocarbon-dated to approximately 25,000 BP, proving symbolic body ornamentation

Detailed Analysis:
Patne yielded fragments of ostrich eggshells engraved with criss-cross geometric designs and finished perforated disc beads, proving symbolic art in India by 25 ka BP.
Therefore, option (D) is the correct answer.

questionText: Microscopic examination of paint droplets on the walls of Lascaux and Chauvet demonstrated that prehistoric artists invented the first 'Airbrush', using:

options.text: Hollow bird bones as blowpipes or spraying mouth-held pigment slurries directly onto rock surfaces
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT principle for Spit and Spray Aerographing.

options.text: Steam-powered paint pumps
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Pressurized aerosol spray paint cans
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Modern pneumatic air compressors driven by electricity
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Archaeological Anthropology (Spit and Spray Aerographing):
Hollow bird bones as blowpipes or spraying mouth-held pigment slurries directly onto rock surfaces

Detailed Analysis:
Cave painters used two hollow bird bones as an atomizer or blew pigment from their mouths, achieving smooth shaded gradient tones across animal flanks.
Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.
